name: Joomla Component Builder
summary: A compiler-oriented development platform for generating native Joomla components, plugins, modules, and supporting code across multiple Joomla generations.
value: JCB turns architecture, schemas, reusable code, and extension metadata into repeatable builds. Its significance is not a single component: it is the maintained system that produces and evolves families of systems.
role: Principal architect and long-term steward since 2014/15; public canonical Git history from 2016.
architecture: Version-aware compilation separates shared intent from Joomla-generation-specific output.
Structured definitions drive extension generation instead of relying on one-off manual assembly.
Reusable Powers and Super Powers give generated systems stable references to shared implementation units.
Build, package, import/export, and repository-sync concerns are designed as parts of one lifecycle.
interfaces: Structured component, field, view, and extension definitions
Generated PHP, JavaScript, XML, SQL, and configuration assets
decisions: Encode repeatable architecture in generators while retaining version-specific output boundaries.
Treat backwards compatibility, upgrade paths, and long-term maintenance as first-class design constraints.
Separate reusable implementation units from any one generated extension.
quality: Versioned releases and public change history
Generated output inspection and package validation
Extensive public documentation and contributor-facing material

name: GetBible v3 publication pipeline
summary: A Python 3.12 build system that converts SWORD module output into a deterministic, validated, checksummed static API.
value: The pipeline creates a controlled publication boundary between native source extraction and downstream consumers. It validates framing and contracts, produces deterministic artifacts, and refuses publication when integrity conditions fail.
architecture: Native SWORD extraction is consumed through a line-oriented NDJSON contract.
Transformation stages normalize content into versioned static API artifacts.
Validation checks framing, schemas, identifiers, checksums, and publication expectations.
Build output is deterministic so releases can be compared, reproduced, and audited.
interfaces: Static API v3 files and indexes
decisions: Use a streaming contract to keep the native and Python responsibilities independently testable.
Fail closed: malformed or incomplete inputs do not become public artifacts.
Preserve stable identifiers and editorial semantics across transformation.

name: GetBibleSWORD
summary: A native C++20 extraction engine for CrossWire SWORD modules with a CLI, stable C ABI, deterministic NDJSON output, and cross-architecture releases.
value: The engine isolates native library concerns behind explicit machine interfaces, allowing build pipelines and other consumers to use SWORD data without inheriting its implementation complexity.
architecture: A native core reads SWORD modules and emits a versioned NDJSON protocol.
The command-line interface supports batch and pipeline operation.
A stable C ABI exposes library functionality to other runtimes without a C++ ABI dependency.
Release workflows target x86_64 and arm64.
decisions: Use C++ for direct SWORD integration and a C ABI for broad language interoperability.
Keep output deterministic and line-oriented for validation, streaming, and failure isolation.
Treat the protocol as a contract rather than an incidental serialization detail.

name: Joomla MCP
summary: A TypeScript MCP server that maps a source-catalogued Joomla Web Services surface into structured tools with guarded write operations.
value: The project connects agent reasoning to a real application platform while keeping tool contracts, write permissions, audit concerns, and transport boundaries explicit.
architecture: Route templates are catalogued from source and projected into MCP tools.
Read and write concerns are separated, with writes placed behind explicit guards.
Transport supports stdio and HTTP integration modes.
Companion and API layers isolate Joomla-specific behavior from protocol concerns.
decisions: Catalogue routes from source instead of relying on an unverified manual list.
Make mutating operations visibly different and explicitly controlled.
Report validation status accurately; a catalogued route is not automatically a production-certified route.
quality: Public validation status and known limits

name: OpenCode Platform
summary: A source-controlled family of Ubuntu 24.04 Incus VM images for PHP, Python, C++, TypeScript, and combined engineering work.
value: The platform makes language environments, agent tooling, and operational boundaries reproducible while keeping credentials and network access outside the image source.
architecture: Layered base, language-specific, and full images keep shared concerns centralized.
Source control is the definition of the environment rather than a manually configured machine.
Joomla MCP integration is available in relevant images without embedding deployment secrets.
Credential and network boundaries are documented as external operational concerns.
decisions: Prefer full virtual-machine isolation where development tasks need system-level tools.
Keep secrets out of images and source-controlled configuration.
Use a compositional image family instead of duplicating every toolchain.

name: Joomla Docker
summary: Official Joomla container image work covering repeatable builds, image variants, multi-architecture publication, and upstream delivery constraints.
value: This work demonstrates framework knowledge at the delivery boundary: the application, runtime, operating image, release process, and official-images requirements must agree.
architecture: Image variants express supported runtime and web-server combinations.
Build definitions track Joomla releases and upstream base images.
Official-images integration adds review and publication constraints beyond a private image build.
decisions: Keep images reproducible and understandable from source.
Support architecture and runtime variants without hiding their differences.
Coordinate application releases with upstream container publication requirements.

name: JCB Super Powers
summary: A central registry of reusable, namespaced PHP classes, interfaces, traits, and abstractions referenced through stable identifiers and injected through JCB.
value: The registry separates reusable architecture from individual generated systems and gives code units a stable identity across projects and build contexts.
architecture: Reusable implementation units are stored independently from consuming extensions.
Stable identifiers allow generators to resolve and inject the required units.
Namespacing and explicit dependencies reduce accidental coupling.
decisions: Make reuse explicit and source-controlled instead of copying code between extensions.
Use stable references so generated projects can evolve independently of registry layout.

name: GetBible Flutter
summary: A typed, local-data-first Flutter reader designed for Android, iOS, web, Windows, macOS, and Linux targets.
value: The project extends the publication architecture into a private, cross-platform client with a typed domain model and local database boundary.
architecture: Typed domain and data layers isolate application behavior from storage and presentation.
Drift and SQLite provide local persistence without requiring an account-based runtime service.
Platform targets share application logic while retaining target-specific packaging.
decisions: Prefer local data and privacy-preserving operation.
Keep development status explicit rather than implying completed store distribution.

name: Joomla project service
summary: A sustained official volunteer record spanning production, infrastructure, strategy, directory, language, testing, mentoring, and leadership responsibilities.
value: The record demonstrates contribution beyond code: maintaining shared systems, coordinating work, reviewing changes, supporting contributors, and participating in project direction.
role: Volunteer, maintainer, mentor, team leader, and strategy contributor across multiple teams.
architecture: Production and infrastructure responsibilities connect framework decisions to operational reality.
Strategy and working-group service connects implementation detail to project-wide direction.
Testing, mentoring, and directory work require cross-team communication and sustained maintenance.
decisions: Treat community systems and documentation as maintained engineering products.
Contribute across code, operations, review, coordination, and teaching.

name: Long-running professional systems
summary: A portfolio of institutional, commercial, workflow, information, and operational systems maintained across long working relationships.
value: The record shows architecture under non-demo conditions: changing requirements, production continuity, hosting, security, data stewardship, support, and maintenance.
role: Independent architect, developer, operator, and technical lead through Vast Development Method.
architecture: Information and workflow systems are designed around the organization’s operating model.
Delivery includes hosting, maintenance, support, recovery, and change management.
Long-lived systems require migration and compatibility decisions as frameworks and infrastructure evolve.
interfaces: Hosting, source control, and secrets infrastructure
decisions: Avoid publishing private client implementation details beyond the supplied professional record.
Represent continuing work by verified relationship and scope, not invented outcomes or metrics.

name: OctoJoom
summary: A substantial Bash control plane for deploying and managing Dockerized Joomla and OpenSSH development environments across Linux, macOS, and Windows.
value: OctoJoom demonstrates Shell engineering as product engineering: operating-system detection, dependency management, persistent configuration, interactive and non-interactive control paths, container lifecycle, update behavior, and clean removal are designed as one maintained system.
role: Original author and long-term maintainer; the repository README directly credits Llewellyn van der Merwe.
architecture: A command dispatcher supports both interactive whiptail operation and explicit flags for repeatable automation.
Persistent environment configuration separates remembered deployment intent from executable Shell logic.
Joomla and OpenSSH container concerns are modelled as related but distinct deployment types.
Operating-system detection selects supported installation and dependency paths while keeping one public command surface.
interfaces: Direct CLI flags and environment values
decisions: Keep the operational logic inspectable in Shell and validate it with ShellCheck.
Provide one tool for guided human use and unattended automation instead of maintaining separate implementations.
Treat update and uninstall behavior as product lifecycle features.
quality: Documented Linux, macOS, and Windows paths
Dry, update, help, and selective-uninstall behaviors

name: JoomEngine container release engine
summary: The official Shell-based Docker image build system for Joomla Component Builder, generating build matrices, manifests, tags, and published images from upstream release evidence.
value: The system makes container publication auditable. Release discovery, integrity hashes, Joomla/PHP/runtime expansion, stable and prerelease tag leadership, generated build contexts, state tracking, and registry publication are implemented in reviewable Shell rather than hidden inside CI YAML.
role: Architect, author, and maintainer of the build engine and release model.
architecture: Upstream JCB release XML is converted into verified release inputs with required SHA-512 hashes.
A declarative compatibility matrix expands Joomla versions, PHP versions, and Apache/FPM runtime variants.
Generated Docker contexts remain output; authoritative behavior lives in the Shell engine and templates.
An NDJSON manifest records each independently buildable image and its complete tag set.
interfaces: Docker build contexts and registry tags
NDJSON build manifest and GitHub Actions
decisions: Keep CI thin so the exact production behavior can be executed and reviewed locally.
Refuse releases without integrity hashes and prevent tag collisions between stable and prerelease channels.
Track processed build combinations to avoid unnecessary registry work.
quality: Dry-run, quiet, force, and build-only modes

name: GetBible engineering ecosystem
summary: A complete public engineering estate spanning Shell and Python builders, static APIs, C/C++ native interfaces, PHP and Python libraries, MCP, Joomla, Telegram, web, desktop, and cross-platform clients.
value: GetBible is not one repository or interface. It is a maintained chain from source-module extraction and integrity validation through versioned publication, language libraries, application APIs, CMS delivery, interactive services, and end-user clients. The public organization shows how those boundaries are designed to evolve independently without losing data integrity.
role: Architect, author, and maintainer across the public GetBible organization; the user has identified every project in the organization as his work.
architecture: Native SWORD extraction is isolated behind deterministic contracts and a stable C ABI.
Versioned builders transform validated inputs into static APIs and integrity manifests.
Language libraries and extensions provide Python, PHP, Shell, TypeScript/MCP, and application-specific boundaries.
Joomla, Telegram, web, desktop, and Flutter surfaces consume maintained service and publication contracts.
interfaces: CrossWire SWORD modules and native ABI
Versioned static JSON APIs and hashes
Python, PHP, Shell, MCP, and JavaScript integration layers
Joomla, Telegram, web, desktop, and Flutter applications
decisions: Keep generated API repositories visible but do not use their data volume as a substitute for source engineering evidence.
Separate extraction, validation, transformation, publication, library, and application responsibilities.
Preserve historical systems and deprecation evidence while directing current consumers to maintained interfaces.
quality: Direct evidence across 28 public organization repositories
Versioned releases, PyPI and native package paths
Public documentation, CI, deployment, and operational tooling

name: Octoleo Shell automation estate
summary: A family of authored Octo-prefixed Shell systems covering repository synchronization, Joomla packaging, reusable-code operations, infrastructure, archives, diagnostics, and delivery.
value: The Octoleo repositories demonstrate repeated productization of operational knowledge. Instead of documenting fragile manual sequences, the projects encode them into reviewable command surfaces with configuration, dry-run behavior, automation paths, and focused responsibilities.
role: Original author and maintainer of the Octo-prefixed projects, JoomEngine, and PlantUML-for-Gitea integration identified by the user.
architecture: OctoSync models repository-to-repository movement through explicit source and target configuration.
Packaging and archive utilities keep release operations small, composable, and callable from larger workflows.
Infrastructure and diagnostic tools encode repeatable operator decisions without requiring an application runtime.
PlantUML-for-Gitea extends developer documentation through a focused browser integration.
interfaces: Git repositories, branches, forks, and pull requests
Joomla packages and JCB reusable-code registries
decisions: Prefer composable utilities with explicit help and inspectable behavior.
Keep public mirrors connected to their primary VDM-hosted source where applicable.
Separate original Octoleo systems from unrelated third-party organization forks.
quality: Direct public links to every identified authored repository
Longitudinal Shell evidence from 2017 through current work

name: TrueChristian publication systems
summary: A focused engineering estate for scheduled Scripture and devotional publication, Joomla delivery, sermon distribution, and print-ready hymn production.
value: These projects connect automation to real publication outputs: scheduled Shell workflows, CMS modules and components, and a Python document-production engine. They show small operational systems and larger publishing products in one maintained domain.
role: Architect, author, and maintainer across the public TrueChristian organization, as identified by the user.
architecture: Shell projects maintain recurring Daily Light, Daily Scripture, and web witness publication.
Joomla modules and the Sermon Distributor connect maintained content streams to CMS delivery.
The Hymn Booklet Generator converts structured Markdown and TOML into reading and imposed print PDFs.
decisions: Keep generated content distinct from the automation and application source that produces it.
Use formats maintainers can author directly while automating layout and distribution.

name: Hymn Booklet Generator
summary: A Python document-production system that transforms simple Markdown hymns into indexed digital booklets and saddle-stitch-imposed print PDFs.
value: The project turns a difficult typography and print-production workflow into a reliable command. It measures content before placement, preserves stanza structure, packs columns, generates indexes and publisher matter, pads signatures, and imposes pages for physical folding and stapling.
architecture: A structured Markdown parser retains title, number, stanza, and optional credit boundaries.
Pre-measurement and greedy packing place complete hymns across two-column pages.
Reading-copy rendering and saddle-stitch imposition are separate output responsibilities.
Publisher metadata remains optional and declarative through TOML.
decisions: Use direct canvas drawing for predictable pagination instead of a layout engine that can split content unexpectedly.
Generate digital and physical-print outputs from one source in a single workflow.
Support diacritics through known fonts and preserve authored line breaks.
quality: Index, credits, publisher pages, and signature padding
Documented print procedure and source format

name: C++ public engineering lineage
summary: Public C++ work includes Conway's Game of Life and Go Fish from 2020, preceding the current GetBibleSWORD native engine and its stable C interoperability boundary.
value: The public chronology matters: recent C++20 work is not the beginning of native-language capability. The smaller 2020 applications provide earlier inspectable evidence; GetBibleSWORD shows how that capability is now applied to ABI design, native dependencies, deterministic protocols, conformance, packaging, and cross-architecture delivery.
role: Author of the public 2020 C++ implementations and architect/developer of the current GetBibleSWORD engine.
architecture: Game of Life models state transitions and simulation rules in a portable CMake project.
Go Fish provides a second public object-oriented C++ application from 2020.
GetBibleSWORD advances the public record into a native engine, CLI, C ABI, and deterministic streaming contract.
interfaces: Stable C ABI and NDJSON protocol
decisions: Present repository dates as the start of public evidence, not the start of professional language experience.
Show progression from smaller applications to maintained native platform infrastructure.
Keep the README's acknowledged starting point for Game of Life visible rather than erasing provenance.
quality: Two directly inspectable C++ repositories from 2020
Current conformance and ABI evidence through GetBibleSWORD
